dimensions.note: Handles no secrets. Runs go, git and just locally and writes files; makes no authenticated call and reads no vault. The one personal value it touches is the Code of Conduct contact, published in the generated repository by design.
All four methods log at info on entry and completion with structured placeholders. No string interpolation into messages; the email argument never reaches a log line.

Errors throw before any write, and pre-flight checks catch misconfiguration before the method body runs at all. runCommand includes the command, arguments, exit code and both streams. render throws naming the unknown variable rather than emitting a hole. A test asserts nothing is written when the code-of-conduct guard fires.

39 tests. The suite covers the pure functions and execute(), but until now it never loaded a workflow — every test drove model methods directly, which is exactly the path that hid three defects: the workflows carried no id UUID and so never registered, the model instance was not shipped for consumers to install, and check_prereqs probed go with --version, a flag go rejects. A workflow is now run end to end during development, and check_prereqs is exercised against the real binaries.

write_files skips an existing file unless overwrite is on, and overwrite reaches generated files only — asserted by test. create_project is idempotent: mkdir is recursive, git init on an existing repository is a no-op. Partial failure leaves partial files a re-run completes rather than conflicts with.
No HTTP call, no external API, no pagination. The only network access in what it produces is the generated justfile's curl, which runs in the generated project.
No sockets, handles or temporary files. Deno.readTextFile and Deno.writeTextFile manage their own handles; Deno.Command output is fully buffered. Filesystem tests clean up in a finally.

CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md shipped the template author's address in its enforcement section, so every consumer would have named a stranger as the person to report harassment to. It takes a variable now, with both a pre-flight check and a guard refusing without one. AI_POLICY.md named an unrelated organization four times and is generic. No IPs, hostnames, subnets or account identifiers. One real URL by design: justfilesRepo, used only when sharedJustfiles is on, which is off by default.
Both schemas are plain z.object with no .passthrough(). Every field typed, and projectName carries a regex rejecting anything Go cannot use as a module or package name.

The one resource spec declares lifetime 'infinite' and garbageCollection 10. Infinite because the record of what a scaffolder wrote is the audit trail for a directory that still exists; 10 versions bounds it.
Not a CRUD lifecycle model. It scaffolds a directory once and optionally re-renders it; no remote resource to update, delete or sync. The four methods are stages of one operation.

Four labelled checks. Two carry 'policy' and apply to every mutating method: a code of conduct must name a contact, and fetching shared recipes requires somewhere to fetch from. Two carry 'live' and are scoped with appliesTo: create_project requires its parent directory, bootstrap requires a go.mod, so running out of order fails with a sentence naming the fix.
One spec, one instance name, written by all four methods with the same shape. A test asserts every state write matches StateSchema field for field.

Three methods hardcoded the file-list fields to [], so bootstrap after write_files erased what had just been recorded. They read prior state forward through readResource now, and a test pins it. No direct dataRepository access.
First version. Nothing published to upgrade from, no migration to declare.
